title: Microsoft Purview: apply default SharePoint library labels to existing files (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap target, administrator-created policy, licensing, limits and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections are to cite the encryption reference and remove the batch-edit checklist instruction that has no corresponding control row.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to apply library default sensitivity labels to existing SharePoint files.
claims.quote: Enables auto-labeling of existing SharePoint files to match the default sensitivity label configured on their document library.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes closing data-at-rest labelling gaps without manual user labelling.
claims.quote: This helps organizations close labeling gaps for data at rest and ensure consistent, secure-by-default protection across SharePoint libraries—without relying on manual user labeling.

claims.claim: Learn documents an administrator-created auto-labeling policy for applying library defaults to existing files.
claims.quote: To extend your default library label deployment to existing files, create an auto-labeling policy that applies the default sensitivity label from each selected SharePoint document library to eligible existing files at rest.

claims.claim: This policy type does not inspect file content to choose a label.
claims.quote: This policy type doesn't inspect file content to choose a label.

claims.claim: The policy evaluates only document libraries with a configured default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: The policy evaluates only SharePoint document libraries that have a default sensitivity label configured, and applies labels only to eligible supported files.

claims.claim: The library default setting alone does not label existing files at rest.
claims.quote: Doesn't apply to existing files at rest in SharePoint.

claims.claim: The library default setting labels eligible newly uploaded files.
claims.quote: any new files uploaded to that library, or existing files edited in the library will have that label applied if they don't already have a sensitivity label, or they have a sensitivity label but with lower priority.

claims.claim: The library default setting labels eligible files when users edit them.
claims.quote: SharePoint applies this label to new files and to files that users edit in the library. Files that already existed in the library before the default label was configured might remain unlabeled.

claims.claim: Applying a default label configured for encryption can change access to older files.
claims.quote: You can grant permissions to specific people so that only they can interact with the labeled content
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels to sources to support the statement about label encryption changing access.

claims.claim: Library defaults do not support labels using user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Let users assign permissions when they apply the label and the checkbox In Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, prompt users to specify permissions is selected. This setting is sometimes referred to as "user-defined permissions".

claims.claim: Library defaults do not support labels with content access expiry other than Never.
claims.quote: some label configurations that apply encryption aren't suitable for SharePoint, and so don't support a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library: ... User access to content expires is set to a value other than Never.

claims.claim: Library defaults do not support labels using Double Key Encryption.
claims.quote: some label configurations that apply encryption aren't suitable for SharePoint, and so don't support a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library: ... Double Key Encryption is selected.

claims.claim: General auto-labeling preserves manually applied labels by default.
claims.quote: Default behavior whether automatic labeling will override an existing label: When content has been manually labeled, that label won't be replaced by automatic labeling.

claims.claim: General auto-labeling replaces lower-priority automatically applied labels.
claims.quote: Automatic labeling will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that was automatically applied, but not a higher priority label.
